notes:
Summary: Closed-lost (decision made 2024-06-01). Primary reason: centralized cloud strategy — procurement chose hyperscaler managed endpoints (GCP Vertex + Cloud AI) to consolidate contracts and monitoring. Secondary reasons: budget reallocation to a multi-year cloud commitment and security team unwilling to adopt third-party private control plane during initial rollout.

Timeline / recent activity:
- 2024-01-11: Lead created from inbound event (webinar). AE assigned (Ava). Initial discovery call on 2024-01-18.
- 2024-02-02: SE deep-dive (Marcus) — architecture fit: VPC-only, customer wants KMS integration and audit logs. POC scope defined (support chat + doc search).
- 2024-03-10: POC kickoff (2-week). We provided test model bundle, batching configs, and cost estimates vs Vertex.
- 2024-03-24: Security questionnaire submitted (SOC2 evidence, KMS flow). Security asked for HSM/KMS mapping and retention controls.
- 2024-04-12: POC results: latency SLOs satisfied (95th p90 < 180ms for demo load), embeddings cost ~18% lower than Vertex baseline in our config. Shared results deck (link in Drive).
- 2024-04-28: Call with CTO + Director of Cloud Ops. Quote: "We love the performance but we have existing enterprise credits and a vendor consolidation mandate." (Fireflies ff_20240428_1122).
- 2024-05-12: Procurement review; legal flagged additional indemnity and data residency language for third-party private control plane (fireflies ff_20240512_0947).
- 2024-05-22: Internal champion (Senior ML Platform Engineer) accepted counter-offer from another team and left — momentum stalls.
- 2024-06-01: Formal procurement decision: choose GCP Vertex managed endpoints; contract executed 2024-06-05.

Detailed notes / quotes:
- Chief Architect (email 2024-05-30): "We are standardizing on GCP for managed model serving — reduces ops surface and aligns with our billing/monitoring stack."
- Security: required vendor to pass additional pentest + extended SLAs; longer timeline than SummitBridge program allowed. Decision: reduce vendor surface area.
- Budget: finance applied 3-year cloud commitment; immediate year 1 funds moved to cloud provider credits.

POC takeaways for Redwood:
- Strengths: demonstrable latency/cost wins; SE team well liked.
- Gaps: procurement friction around third-party control plane and contract templates; lack of a strong sponsor after champion left.

Next actions / followups if re-engage:
- Target Q4 re-engagement aligning with their renewal planning for cloud credits.
- Provide whitepaper / legal-friendly contract language for customers with cloud consolidation mandates.
- Offer an architecture note for hybrid deployment: Redwood Private control plane but with cloud-brokered billing integration (to appease procurement).

- Security FAQ: drive:/RD/SummitBridge/security-FAQ.pdf
- Fireflies transcripts: ff_20240428_1122, ff_20240512_0947
